case_study_insert.main_stem: Brightpath Tuition Partners (BTP) is a partnership in the private tutoring sector, employing a workforce of 36. Founded in 2014 by Kwame Mensah and Lena Fischer, BTP operates one city-centre institute offering after-school tuition and exam preparation, using a flat structure with autocratic leadership. It plans to invest $380,000 in a second campus in Northgate, financed by a $120,000 hire-purchase agreement for teaching technology and $260,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $120,000 a year, a variable cost of $4.00 a unit and a selling price of $14.00, and currently produces 25,000 units a year. BTP faces difficult recruitment of qualified tutors, tutor turnover of 21%, complaints about timetable clashes, and a waiting list of 210 places for maths and sciences.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations and Quality Report — Q3 2025: The institute delivered 6,250 tuition units last quarter at an on-time rate of 94.5%, up from 91.2% a year ago. Student complaints fell from 18 to 11 per month. A survey of 600 parents found 69% reported mock-exam score improvement, 54% want an admissions-test programme and 46% would pay up to $45 more per month for small-group science classes. A waiting list of 210 places covers maths and sciences; 9 of 36 tutors have not completed the new online marking system training. Off-the-job training at the professional institute costs $540 per tutor.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Brightpath Tuition Partners for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.75% to 5.5%, increasing borrowing costs and monthly payments for businesses with hire-purchase agreements. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 7.4% from $12.50 to $13.42 per hour from April 2026, raising support-staff wage bills. (3) Tutor agency and software licensing costs have risen 8.8% year-on-year, education inflation is running at 5.9%, and consumer spending on after-school tutoring grew 6.3% in the same period.

questions.question_text: BTP plans to finance part of its Northgate campus with hire purchase. Explain two advantages for BTP of using retained profit to fund the expansion instead of hire purchase.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Using retained profit costs BTP nothing in hire charges or interest, protecting the partners' cash flow at a time when fixed costs of $120,000 a year are already absorbed by the single city-centre institute. Every dollar kept inside the business can absorb the 8.8% rise in tutor agency and software licensing costs and help BTP hold its $14.00 session price while it builds Northgate against a waiting list of 210 places in maths and sciences.

Point 2: Retained profit avoids the hire-purchase schedule on the $120,000 of teaching technology — no risk of equipment being repossessed if Northgate fills slowly, and no hire agreement constraining the partners' choices. It also keeps Kwame Mensah and Lena Fischer's shared ownership and direct, autocratic direction intact, since no finance company can dictate tuition methods, class sizes or the small-group science classes that 46% of the 600 parents surveyed would pay up to $45 more per month for.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to Brightpath Tuition Partners, its Northgate campus and its financing choice.

questions.question_text: BTP is promoting its new Northgate campus. Consider local press advertising, regional radio sponsorship, or social media advertising aimed at parents. Which should BTP choose to promote the campus? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Local press advertising: Local press would build credible presence in the Northgate community and reach parents of exam-age children who still read newspapers, and response slips can pull trial bookings. However, readership is declining, much of the coverage lies outside BTP's realistic catchment, and the cost per enquiry is hard to track, so wastage is significant for a 36-tutor partnership funding a $380,000 second campus partly with retained profit.

Regional radio sponsorship: Regional radio is cheaper than television, reaches commuting parents on the Northgate approach roads, and suits a time-limited launch offer such as a free trial lesson. However, reach is broad but blunt; radio cannot target exam subjects or a specific catchment, and it cannot capture bookings directly, so converting awareness into filled classes would still be slow while the waiting list of 210 places needs clearing methodically.

Social media advertising aimed at parents: Social media lets BTP geo-target Northgate postcodes and promote the 69% of 600 surveyed parents reporting mock-exam score improvement, the 54% demanding an admissions-test programme and the $45 small-group science offer. It is measurable per enquiry, allows retargeting of booking-page visitors and reinforces BTP's exam-focused positioning, though it depends on quick replies to parent messages and enough tutor capacity to take the trials it generates.

Recommendation: BTP should choose social media advertising aimed at parents. It reaches exactly the segment identified in BTP's own research, is cheapest per enquiry and reinforces the 69% exam-improvement story with measurable follow-through. Local press is rejected as untargeted and hard to measure; regional radio is rejected as too broad and unable to target subject-level demand — both can play supporting awareness roles, but neither should lead the launch.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited knowledge or outline of the promotional options with minimal context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of BTP with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options in the context of BTP with a well-justified recommendation explaining why the press campaign and radio sponsorship are rejected.

questions.question_text: BTP's tutor turnover has reached 21%. Explain two benefits for BTP of introducing democratic leadership to improve motivation in its tutoring team.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership would invite the 36 tutors to help shape timetabling, class grouping, marking standards and the Northgate rollout, rather than simply receiving instructions from Kwame Mensah and Lena Fischer. Giving tutors a genuine voice raises job satisfaction and meets social and esteem needs, reducing the frustration behind 21% turnover and helping BTP stabilise the maths and science teams that serve the 210-place waiting list; democratic forums would also surface the timetable clashes parents complain about before they harden into refunds or lost referrals.

Point 2: Involving tutors generates practical ideas from those who deliver 6,250 tuition units last quarter at a 94.5% on-time rate, up from 91.2%. Tutor-led fixes to timetable clashes (complaints already down from 18 to 11 per month), the 9 of 36 tutors pending online-marking training and parents' requests for admissions-test preparation could cut turnover further, reduce recruitment costs for qualified tutors and protect output of 25,000 units a year as the campus opens; lower churn also protects the consistency parents notice when scores move.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to BTP's turnover, punctuality, waiting list and output.

questions.question_text: BTP must train the 9 tutors who have not completed the new online marking system. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training at the professional institute. Which should BTP choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Training beside experienced tutors using the actual online marking system is directly relevant to BTP's own marking rubrics, feedback turnaround and parent reports, costs no fees and keeps the 9 tutors teaching — vital with a 210-place waiting list and 94.5% on-time delivery to protect. However, it depends on senior-tutor availability, can pass on inconsistent marking habits, and gives no external certificate that some parents and schools look for.

Off-the-job training at the professional institute: College courses at $540 per tutor give structured, up-to-date digital-marking skills and formal certificates for all 9 tutors at $4,860 in total — modest against a $380,000 expansion and $120,000 of fixed costs. However, tutors are removed from sessions for days at a time, classes must be covered or rearranged against timetable pressure, content is generic rather than matched to BTP's exact system, and cover costs add strain for a 36-strong workforce — especially in exam season, when marking demand peaks and even a single absent tutor backs up dozens of scripts.

Decision: BTP should choose on-the-job training for the 9 tutors, reserving college attendance for the two senior tutors who will cascade the skills. On-the-job delivery is system-specific, free and avoids worsening the waiting list or timetable clashes; full off-the-job training is rejected because $4,860 plus 9 absent tutors would compress delivery against the evening peak and Northgate opening. Certificates can be added later through short refreshers once the campus stabilises, and the college days can be staggered across two school-holiday intakes so every Northgate class stays covered without cancelling a single session.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to BTP.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of both training methods in the context of BTP.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both training methods in the context of BTP with a well-justified decision covering cost, waiting list, system relevance and the Northgate launch.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how BTP's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $120,000 ÷ ($14.00 − $4.00) = $120,000 ÷ $10.00 = 12,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 12,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $14.00 − $4.00 = $10.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $10.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways BTP's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 12,000-unit break-even output with actual output of 25,000 units to confirm the institute is comfortably profitable with a margin of safety of 13,000 units, informing how aggressively the Northgate campus should open and hire.
2. Use contribution per unit of $10.00 to model fee changes or the $45 small-group science premium: adding $45 a month lifts contribution sharply, letting managers judge whether the 46% of parents wanting small-group classes can fund the extra tutor hires against the 21% turnover.
3. Check that the $120,000 hire-purchase agreement on teaching technology is serviceable by verifying the 13,000-unit margin of safety against the 8.8% rise in software licensing before committing to the $380,000 Northgate investment.
4. Benchmark unit cost ($120,000 ÷ 25,000 units + $4.00 = $8.80 a unit) across tutors to spot underperforming groups, attack the 11-complaint-a-month trend and track productivity of roughly 694 units per tutor per year for review conversations.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 12,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $10.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety of 13,000 units against 25,000-unit output; fee and premium modelling against the $120,000 fixed costs; serviceability checking for the $120,000 hire-purchase agreement funding teaching technology; unit-cost benchmarking at $8.80 and per-tutor productivity to drive Northgate hiring.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate BTP's financial performance by calculating the gross profit margin, the profit margin and ROCE for 2024 and 2025. Has BTP's financial performance improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 55.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 58.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 15.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 18.0%
ROCE 2024 = 18.0%
ROCE 2025 = 21.0%

Detailed workings: 2024 gross profit $165,000 on revenue $300,000 (cost of sales $135,000); 2025 gross profit $203,000 on revenue $350,000 (cost of sales $147,000). 2024 operating profit $45,000; 2025 operating profit $63,000. 2024 capital employed $250,000; 2025 capital employed $300,000. Interest payable rose from $9,000 to $13,000, reflecting the hire-purchase agreement on teaching technology.

Evaluation: Performance improved steadily. Revenue grew $50,000 (16.7%) — consistent with 25,000 tuition units at $14.00 — while cost of sales rose just 8.9% to $147,000, lifting gross profit from $165,000 to $203,000 (23.0%); the on-time rate also recovered from 91.2% to 94.5%, showing service quality supported the gain. Operating profit grew 40.0% ($45,000 to $63,000), well ahead of revenue growth, so overheads were absorbed efficiently. Capital employed rose $50,000 towards Northgate, yet the return on capital still strengthened from 18.0% to 21.0%. However, the 8.8% agency and software licensing inflation could squeeze 2026 costs, and Northgate ramp-up plus 21% turnover may pressure these results before scale benefits arrive.

Conclusion: Yes, BTP's financial performance has improved. Revenue, gross profit and operating profit all rose, and the return on capital employed climbed from 18.0% to 21.0%, driven by cost control and modest pricing power rather than debt. The judgement is not risk-free — licensing inflation and staffing risks persist — so BTP should lock favourable software terms, retain key tutors and monitor Northgate's conversions closely.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, the profit margin and ROCE for both 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratio calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of revenue, cost of sales, interest and capital employed movements and a justified conclusion on whether BTP's financial performance improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for BTP of introducing small-group science classes at the Northgate campus.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Small-group science classes answer the 46% of the 600 parents surveyed who would pay up to $45 more per month for them, letting Northgate charge a premium that protects the $10.00 contribution per unit while licensing costs inflate 8.8%. The offer strengthens BTP's exam-focused positioning, helps clear the 210-place waiting list in maths and sciences, builds the word-of-mouth referrals Northgate needs, while consumer spending on after-school tutoring grew 6.3% and families actively hunt for exam-proven tutors.

Disadvantage: Small-group classes need qualified science tutors at a time when recruitment is difficult and turnover is 21%, raising variable costs if classes run below healthy sizes. Any failure in lesson quality or exam-preparation delivery could reverse the improvement in mock-exam scores reported by 69% of parents, damage BTP's reputation in a competitive Northgate market, strain the $380,000 Northgate investment before the campus reaches profitability, and risk inconsistent marking across parallel classes if hiring lags.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to BTP's research data, costs and Northgate investment.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 5.5%, the 7.4% minimum wage increase and the 8.8% rise in tutor agency and software licensing costs will affect BTP. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.75% to 5.5%): A 0.75 percentage point increase adds about $900 a year on a $120,000 hire-purchase agreement, lifting BTP's financing cost and edging the interest charge above $13,000. Higher rates also make the remaining funding need for the $380,000 Northgate campus more expensive and could dampen parents' willingness to fund paid tuition; the direct cash hit is the smallest of the three changes, and BTP can negotiate fixed hire terms.

Minimum wage increase (7.4%, to $13.42 per hour): Most tutors earn well above the minimum wage, so perhaps 8 support staff (reception, admin, facilities) are affected. On $13.42 an hour for about 2,000 hours a year, the increase is about $1,850 per affected worker, or roughly $14,800 a year across 8 staff — noticeable against 2025 operating profit of $63,000, but absorbable through rota efficiency and admin productivity gains.

Input cost inflation (8.8% agency and software licensing): BTP relies on tutor agency cover for roughly $180,000 a year of sessions plus software licensing of around $35,000 a year. An 8.8% rise adds about $15,800 on agency cover and roughly $3,100 on licensing — about $18,900 a year of lost contribution in aggregate, striking every session delivered and undermining the model behind the online marking system on which 9 tutors are still pending training.

Conclusion: The 8.8% rise in tutor agency and software licensing costs will have the greatest impact. It strikes both sides of BTP's teaching delivery — labour cover and the digital platform — at roughly $18,900 a year, comfortably exceeding the roughly $14,800 wage impact and dwarfing the $900 interest rise, and it hits precisely as BTP depends on agency cover to fill Northgate. The wage increase is the second most serious risk; the interest rise is smallest, though all three demand tighter purchasing, retention and fixed-rate financing.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to BTP.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on BTP's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes in the context of BTP with a well-justified judgement that agency and software licensing inflation has the greatest impact, and why the wage rise and the interest rise are smaller.
